Paid Install moved the most on its own (-145, -28.8%) and is now 100.0% of all installs, so that is the channel to look at first.

android.head: App Total Revenue -8.1% does not match new subs +38.9% from 7 days earlier — this drop is not coming from new customers.
android.body: App Total Revenue on 10-07 vs 09-30 is -8.1%, but App Total New Subs on 09-30 vs 09-23 was +38.9% — they moved in opposite directions. Most new subs start as a 7-day free trial, so the revenue landing now mostly comes from people who subscribed about 7 days ago. Since those subs went the other way, this drop is coming from existing customers instead: check renewals and cancellations, refunds, or a recent price change — not marketing or installs.

android.head: App Total New User is moving faster than the other steps (-6.4% vs about -21.0%).
android.body: App Total New User is -6.4% while the other steps are all moving about -21.0% — a gap of +14.6pp. When one step moves very differently from the rest, the cause is usually specific to that step.

android.head: No big App Total Revenue swing expected in about 7 days — the share of installs that become subs is normal.
android.body: App Total New Subs is -21.0% and App Total Install is -28.8%; the gap between them (+7.8pp) is under the 10pp we treat as a real signal, so the share of people who install and then subscribe is close to normal. New subs start as 7-day free trials, so today's new subs are next period's App Total Revenue. So nothing unusual is building up that would swing App Total Revenue in about 7 days.
